_comment: GENERATED by scripts/method-inventory.py. Do not edit by hand.
This is the ENUMERATED method inventory for MCP and A2A, expanded into the
method x direction x transport matrix. crates/busbar/tests/method_coverage.rs
reads it and FAILS the build for any cell that is neither implemented nor
A cell with an na_reason is not owed an implementation. A cell WITHOUT one is,
and its absence from the status file is a MISSING -- which is a build failure,

methods.derived_from: rmcp 3.1.2 const ElicitationResponseNotificationMethod (rmcp declares ElicitationResponseNotificationMethod but lists it in no ts_union!; SEP-1036 sends the elicitation response from client to server)

not derivable: A2A SPEC 8.2 and the IANA registration in SPEC 14.3 define the Agent Card as an HTTP resource. It is not an rpc in service A2AService, so a proto-only derivation misses it entirely -- and it is the FIRST thing every A2A client fetches.

na.grpc: The card is an HTTP resource at a well-known path, not an rpc; gRPC has no well-known-path concept and the proto service block does not declare it. A gRPC-only peer discovers busbar via the same HTTP fetch.

methods.derived_from: not derivable: Delivering a push notification is the agent POSTing a Task to the client's webhook URL. It is an obligation of the server role with no rpc, no JSON-RPC method and no gRPC form -- so it is invisible to the service block even though three TCK MUSTs judge it.

na.jsonrpc: Delivery is an outbound HTTP POST to the client's webhook. There is no JSON-RPC request for it; the JSON-RPC binding only carries the CONFIG methods.
na.grpc: Same: the proto declares the config messages, never a delivery rpc.

methods.derived_from: not derivable: Opening the server-to-client SSE stream, and resuming it with Last-Event-ID, is a streamable-HTTP transport obligation with no JSON-RPC method name, so an rmcp-model-only derivation cannot see it. Without it NO server-originated request or notification can reach the client over HTTP.

na.stdio: stdio has no session envelope and no second channel: the stream IS the process's stdout, opened once at spawn.

methods.derived_from: not derivable: Explicit session termination is a streamable-HTTP verb, not a JSON-RPC method. It is the only way a client can tell a gateway to drop server-side state it is being billed for.

na.stdio: A stdio session ends when the process does; there is no session id to delete.
